questions.question: Which of the following musical instruments is also known as a ‘Mangal Vadya’?
questions.solution:

Shehnai:

 
• It is a reed instrument in which there are seven holes along the tube which are used for playing the melody by opening and closing them with the fingers. 
 
• It is known as a Mangal Vadya and is usually played on all auspicious occasions in north India such as marriages, temple festivals, etc.
 
• The Shehnai is considered to have come to India from West Asia, there are other scholars who believe that this instrument travelled to China from India.
 
• It is now a popular instrument in concerts, the sound is very sweet and suited for playing Raga Sangeet.
 
• In the early fifties of this century, Ustad Bismillah Khan is credited for popularizing this instrument. 
 
• Today, Pt. Anant Lal and Pt. Daya Shankar is also a noted **Shehnai player.**

questions.question: Right to Information Act ______ mandates timely response to citizen requests for government information.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2005.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

 
• **Right to Information (RTI),2005, **is an act set up by the Parliament of India that frames the procedures and rules for the right to information to the citizen.
 
• **RTI** has replaced the Freedom of information act, 2002.

**The following are the features of the RTI Act:**

 
• It promotes accountability and transparency in every public authority.
 
• It promotes effective and timely dissemination of correct information by the public authority to any individual.
 
• It promotes the establishment of district, state, and central level information commissions as an appellate body.
 
• **It** may be written by** hand or online.**
 
• To maintain all the records which are appropriate to be computerized and should be connected with the network so that all the records are easily accessible.
 
• To prepare reports which include the number of report requests made by the general public to each authority.
 
• It is transparent and shows the amount collected by public authority as a charge from this act.

questions.question: Which one of the following words does not come before the word 'Republic' in the Preamble of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ **Federal.**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The preamble is the introductory part of the Constitution which sets out the principles on which the Constitution is based.
 
• **The preamble declares India to be a sovereign, socialist, secular and democratic republic.**
 
• The word **Federal is nowhere mentioned in the Indian** constitution.
 
• The ideals behind the Preamble to India’s Constitution were laid down by **Jawaharlal Nehru’s Objectives Resolution,** adopted by the** Constituent Assembly on January 22, 1947**.
 
• The date is mentioned in the preamble when it was adopted i.e. **November 26, 1949.**

**Keywords in Preamble**__

 
• **We, the people of India: **

 
 
• It indicates the ultimate sovereignty of the people of India.
 
 
 
• **Sovereign:**
 
 
• The term means that India has its own independent authority and it is not a dominion of any other external power.
 
 
 
• **Socialist:**
 
 
• The term means the achievement of socialist ends through democratic means.
 
• It holds faith in a mixed economy where both private and public sectors co-exist side by side.
 
• **It was added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.**
 
 
 
• **Secular:**
 
 
• The term means that all the religions in India get equal respect, protection and support from the state.
 
• It was incorporated into the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment, 1976.
 
 
 
• **Democratic:**
 
 
• The term implies that the Constitution of India has an established form of Constitution which gets its authority from the will of the people expressed in an election
 
 
 
• **Republic: **
 
 
• **​**The term indicates that the head of the state is elected by the people.
 
• In India, the President of India is the elected head of the state.

questions.question: Which of the following is a group of islands found in the tropical oceans consisting of coral reefs and a central depression?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A**____**toll**__.

__
 
• **Atoll is a group of islands found in the tropical oceans consisting of coral reefs and a central depression​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **An atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef, island, or series of islets.**
 
• An atoll surrounds a body of water called a lagoon.
 
• The term **“atoll” **is derived from a Maldivian (divehi) word, atolu.
 
• Atolls develop with underwater volcanoes, called seamounts.
 
• Atolls consist of ribbons of reefs that may not always be circular but whose broad configuration is a closed shape up to dozens of kilometres across.
 
• The most extensive groups of atolls occur in the Pacific Ocean but there are also numerous atolls in the central Indian Ocean.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 Term
 Meaning
 
 

 Trenches
 A trench is a type of excavation or depression in the ground that is generally deeper than it is wide (as opposed to a wider gully, or ditch), and narrow compared with its length.
 
 

 Seamounts
 
 
Seamounts are underwater mountains that rise hundreds or thousands of feet from the seafloor.

 
They are generally extinct volcanoes that, while active, created piles of lava that sometimes break the ocean surface.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT abiotic?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plant**__.

__
 
• Biotic Factor:__

 __
 
• The word ‘biotic’ refers to having to do with living organisms.
 
• They refer to the biological component of the ecosystem, consisting of a population of plants, animals and micro-organisms in complex communities.
 
• The biotic factors influencing an organism, viruses and other parasitic organisms cause diseases.
 
• These are all parts of an organism’s biotic environment.
 
• The biotic component consists of three distinct groups of organisms, producers, consumers and decomposers.
 
• Examples of biotic factors are fungi, bacteria, yeast, etc.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Abiotic Factor:

 
 
• Factors other than the biotic factors which are important for the atmosphere are called abiotic factors.
 
• Other physical factors include climate, temperature, precipitation, types of soil present (sandy or clay, dry or wet, fertile or infertile), and wind.
 
• In the ecosystem, the abiotic (non-living) components perform the important function of providing water and oxygen for organisms.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a chemical coagulant used in water treatment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nitrogen dioxide.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**Chemical Wastewater Treatment

 
• The chemical used in this process is Aluminium Sulfate (Alum), Polyaluminium chloride (PAC), and Aluminium chloride.
 
• Chemicals are used during wastewater treatment in an array of processes to expedite disinfection.
 
• **Specialized chemicals such as chlorine, hydrogen peroxide, sodium chlorite, and sodium hypochlorite (bleach) act as agents that disinfect, sanitize, and assist in the purification of wastewater at treatment facilities.**
 
• There are several distinct chemical unit processes that can be applied to wastewater during cleaning.
 
 
• Chemical coagulation
 
• Chemical precipitation
 
• Chemical oxidation
 
• Advanced oxidation
 
• Ion exchange
 
• Chemical neutralization and stabilization
 
 
 
• The** chemical coagulant process involves destabilizing wastewater particles **so that they aggregate during chemical flocculation.
 
• Fine solid particles dispersed in wastewater carry negative electric surface charges (in their normal stable state), which prevent them from forming larger groups and settling.
 
• Chemical coagulation destabilizes these particles by introducing positively charged coagulants that then reduce the negative particles’ charge.

questions.question: According to World Health Organization (WHO), “Hygiene refers to ______ and practices that help to maintain ______ and ______ the spread of diseases.”
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**conditions, **health, prevent.__

__
 
• According to World Health Organization (WHO), “Hygiene refers to conditions and practices that help to maintain health and prevent the spread of diseases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hygiene **refers to conditions and practices that help to maintain health and prevent the spread of diseases.
 
• Medical hygiene, therefore, includes a specific set of practices associated with this preservation of health, for example, environmental cleaning, sterilization of equipment, hand hygiene, water and sanitation and safe disposal of medical waste.
 
• Personal hygiene refers to maintaining the body's cleanliness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Working with 194 Member States across 6 regions and on the ground in 150+ locations, the WHO team works to improve everyone’s ability to enjoy good health and well-being.
 
• India is a member of WHO.​
 
• **Establishment:** April 7th, 1948
 
• **Headquarters: **Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.question: Who among the following won the 2020 JCB Prize for Literature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**S Hareesh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• Malayalam author S Hareesh__ won the coveted JCB Prize for Literature 2020 for his novel, ‘Moustache’.
 
• Translated in English by Jayasree Kalathil and published by HarperCollins India, the book has been praised for its impeccable confluence of myth and magic.
 
• The winner was announced by JCB chairman Lord Bamford in a virtual ceremony.
 
• The prize, worth Rs 25 lakh, is one of the most prestigious literary awards in India.
